why: The criterion holds: I found no check whose PASS or FAIL conditions go beyond the words of its expect line. Check 1 tests argument order, the `<file>:<line>: <error>` format and behaviour matching the old single-file case. Check 2 tests that stdin is reported as `-` and that `- -` exits 2. Check 3 tests the 0/1/2 exit codes, the stderr error and that "other files still checked and reported". Its missing+bad exit code is only in the PASS condition loosely; the precedence rule is under Advisory. Check 4 asks only that the lint function has no changes. The stricter byte-identical file comparison is under Advisory. Check 5 lists exactly the required test cases and README usage. Check 6 covers the PR body, npm test and the workflow. Under Advisory: stdout must be empty for usage errors, newlines in errors must be flattened, and the exit-code expectations. One borderline point: "nothing for ok.jsonl" and the clean-stdin "prints nothing" follow from "as for one file before".
